To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found that the expression of several genes involved in Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis is altered in relation with increasing Alzheimer's disease pathology in the brain.

we have identified changes in gene expression and splicing of several AD risk genes in relation to AD-related neurof fibrillary pathology, and in vitro pathway analysis suggests that FRMD4 is involved in AD-related pathways.

1) The expression of FRMDA4, MS4A, CLU and TREML2 is altered in postmortem brain samples in relation to increasing neurofibrillary tangle pathology; 2) The expression of these genes is not altered in normal pressure hydrocephalous patients; 3) FRMDA4 may be involved in amyloidogenic processing and tau phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of genetic risk factors for Alzheimer's disease (the most common form of dementia) in the disease pathogenesis and development of novel therapeutic targets.
the identification of genes involved in AD, and the investigation of their expression in human brain samples.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of genes associated with the risk of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is altered with the increasing neurofibrillary degeneration in AD.
our data suggest that the expression level of FRMD4a, MS4A, CLU and TREMs is altered in relation with AD-related neurof fibrillary pathology.
the expression of CLU, TREM2 and MS4A6a is altered in AD brain and the downregulation of the FRMD4a may play a role amyloidogenic and taupathological pathways in AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the expression of 4 genes, FRMD4A and MS4A6 in the brain, and CLU and TREMS in the brain and cell culture, is altered in AD and that these genes may be involved in amyloidogenic pathways and/or neurofibrillary tangle formation.

we have found that the expression of several AD risk genes is altered in relation with the progression of AD-related neurodegeneration, and that FRM4D is a novel AD risk gene that may play a role through its effects on amyloidogenic and neurofibrillary tau pathways.
we identified genes whose expression changes in relation to AD-related neurof fibrillary pathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression and splicings of the studied AD risk genes were altered with increasing AD-related neurodegenerative pathology in the postmortems and that these changes were independent of the presence of brain amyloid-positivity.
the expression of the studied genes was altered in relation to AD-related pathology in the human brain, and that FRDM4A may play role in amyloid-β and tau-related pathways.
the expression of several AD risk genes is affected by AD-related pathology in the brain and that these genes may be involved in the amyloidogenic or tau-related pathways.
